facts.claim: The Sugar Research Foundation (SRF) funded a review in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1965 that discounted evidence linking sucrose consumption to blood lipid levels and coronary heart disease.
facts.quote: In 1965, the Sugar Research Foundation (SRF) secretly funded a review in the New England Journal of Medicine that discounted evidence linking sucrose consumption to blood lipid levels and hence coronary heart disease (CHD).

facts.claim: The sugar industry sponsored a research program in the 1960s and 1970s that successfully cast doubt about the hazards of sucrose while promoting fat as the dietary culprit in CHD.
facts.quote: our findings suggest the industry sponsored a research program in the 1960s and 1970s that successfully cast doubt about the hazards of sucrose while promoting fat as the dietary culprit in CHD.

facts.claim: Industry-related studies were overwhelmingly more likely to reach 'weak/null' conclusions compared with independent studies regarding the adverse effects of SSB consumption on health (OR=57·30, 95 % CI 7·12, 461·56).
facts.quote: Industry-related studies were overwhelmingly more likely to reach 'weak/null' conclusions compared with independent studies regarding the adverse effects of SSB consumption on health (OR=57·30, 95 % CI 7·12, 461·56).

facts.claim: The sugar industry did not disclose evidence of harm from animal studies that would have strengthened the case that the CHD risk of sucrose is greater than starch.
facts.quote: The sugar industry did not disclose evidence of harm from animal studies that would have (1) strengthened the case that the CHD risk of sucrose is greater than starch

facts.claim: A study comparing conventional rats fed a high-sugar diet to those fed a high-starch diet suggested that sucrose consumption might be associated with elevated levels of beta-glucuronidase.
facts.quote: A study comparing conventional rats fed a high-sugar diet to those fed a high-starch diet suggested that sucrose consumption might be associated with elevated levels of beta-glucuronidase

facts.claim: The proportion of industry-related scientific studies decreased significantly with time, from approximately 30 % at the beginning of the study period to <5 % towards the end (P=0·003).
facts.quote: The proportion of industry-related scientific studies decreased significantly with time, from approximately 30 % at the beginning of the study period to <5 % towards the end (P=0·003).

research.angle: The sugar industry sponsored research in the 1960s and 1970s that successfully cast doubt on the hazards of sucrose while promoting fat as the primary cause of coronary heart disease.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that the sugar industry actively funded and influenced research to downplay the risks of sucrose and shift the blame for heart disease toward fat.
research.caveat: The research on the health effects of sugar-sweetened beverages shows a significant decrease in industry-related studies over time.
